beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string (Mongo URI) only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or commit it, and never write it to logs or files.
Enable TLS in the Mongo client (tls=true / ssl=true) and require certificate validation; do not connect with insecure TLS settings.

Use connection pooling and set sensible driver options (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) appropriate for concurrent multi-agent workload; tune pools to match number of agent worker threads/processes.
Implement robust retry semantics for transient errors and throttling: exponential backoff, jitter, idempotent-safe retries, and respect 429/Retry-After headers returned by the service.

Avoid multi-document transactions where possible; design updates to be single-document atomic (use $inc/$set) or use application-level compensation, because distributed transactions are limited/expensive on managed DocumentDB/Mongo APIs.

Choose a partition key that aligns with query patterns and evenly distributes load (e.g., account_id or tenant_id), and create collections with partitioning configured up front rather than trying to repartition later.

Create indexes for the exact fields used in filters and the early $match stages of aggregation pipelines (compound indexes when queries filter on multiple fields); verify with explain() that the index is used.

For vector search, store embeddings as a single array field with fixed dimensionality and create the vector index (HNSW/IVF) with the matching dimension and chosen metric (cosine/innerProduct/Euclidean) before running similarity queries.

When running heavy aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project stages as early as possible to reduce working set, use allowDiskUse when needed for large groups/sorts, and monitor RU consumption for the pipeline.
Seed collections using bulkWrite/bulk insert with unordered operations for speed; handle duplicate-key errors gracefully and make seed scripts idempotent by upserting on unique keys.

Store each stress-test run as an immutable audit document with fields: run_id, created_at (ISO8601), schema_version, scenario_parameters, agent_outputs (raw), aggregated_results, run_status, and provenance (user/service), so runs are auditable and replayable.
Include a schema_version field on persisted documents and migrate readers (or write migration code) so stored stress_run documents remain readable as the app evolves.

Limit document size to avoid service document size limits (keep documents small—store large binary blobs or long histories in separate storage like blob storage and reference them), and design audits to avoid exceeding the database item size cap.
Monitor RU/s, request charge per query, index usage, latency, and throttling metrics in Azure Monitor and instrument the app to log RU costs returned by the server for expensive aggregation runs.

Secure credentials using Azure Key Vault or equivalent secret manager; do not place primary keys in source control or test fixtures; use environment-specific config placeholders (.env.example) for onboarding.
Use explain() or the MCP server tools to inspect aggregation query plans when tuning pipelines or indexes; check whether stage is COLLSCAN vs IXSCAN and iterate on index design accordingly.

Guard against hot partitions and skewed RU consumption by avoiding very low-cardinality partition keys (e.g., a single constant value) and by designing queries to include the partition key where possible.
Prefer Session consistency (or the appropriate lower-latency consistency) for application throughput, and only opt for strong consistency when strictly required by correctness/audit semantics.

Use private network access controls (IP firewall rules, VNet/private endpoint) to limit database access to your CI/dev machine and build environment rather than leaving the cluster open to the internet.

In unit tests prefer lightweight mocks for DB calls or run integration tests against an isolated live test database; avoid mocking patterns that create a new MagicMock on every __getitem__ (which breaks dictionary-style access) — return a stable fake document or use mongomock/mini cluster.
